newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech opposition lists 1997 budget conditions.
newsitem.headline: Czech opposition lists 1997 budget conditions.

text.p: Milos Zeman, the leader of the strongest Czech opposition party the Social Democrats (CSSD), said on Thursday his party might support the government draft 1997 budget, but with conditions, the CTK agency reported.

CTK quoted Zeman as saying CSSD wanted the government to tighten measures on tax evasion and economic crime to back the cabinet's draft budget in the parliament, where the government is two votes shy of a majority.

Zeman said CSSD also wanted to halt the planned deregulation of heating prices and state housing rents until a rational energy and housing policy was clear and compensation was available, CTK reported.

Zeman became chairman of parliament in July in a tenous deal that allowed Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus to form a minority government after inconclusive elections with the tacit suppport of the centre-left CSSD.

CTK quoted Zeman as also demanding a cut to the growing state bureaucracy as a condition for approving the budget, which was passed last month by the cabinet and is expected to have a first reading later this month in parliament.
"If this government wants to build new buildings for district offices, then we want to build new hospitals and schools," Zeman was quoted as saying.

Traditionally, the annual Czech budget gets its final reading in December, but Czech media have been ripe with speculation that the CSSD might try to scuttle the budget in an attempt to bring down Klaus's government. Officially, CSSD said it will hold back comment on its final support on the budget until it sees how the government addresses its other concerns.
